title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Server Ping Architecture
purpose: Define the accepted WebSocket tunnel helper boundary for server-sent ping control frames that keep the tunnel available for pong and later data messages.
design_summary: `Http3WebSocketTunnelContext.PingAsync` writes an unmasked server-to-client WebSocket ping control frame using the existing frame writer. The helper does not complete, reset, or otherwise terminate the stream; the application handler remains responsible for reading any pong and later tunnel data.
data_and_state_considerations: The helper introduces no scheduler or connection-level state. Payload size and control-frame finality remain enforced by the shared WebSocket frame writer.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The helper leaves stream lifetime under handler control.
The same tunnel remains available for a pong response and later data messages.
Automatic keepalive scheduling remains out of scope.
risks: Application callers can overread the helper as automatic keepalive policy if the manual boundary is not kept explicit.
Live external WebSocket-over-H3 peer proof remains future work.
